reviewers.summary: The worker route and exact decoded-limit acceptance test are restored. The preflight still has a reachable CPU exhaustion path when scanning repeated `stream` tokens in comments.

findingList.message: Raw `stream` tokens in comments trigger repeated input scans during preflight, leaving a CPU exhaustion path (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: Parse calls CheckStreamLimits before starting the worker. Its loop finds raw `stream` tokens without skipping PDF comments, then searches backward for `endobj` and forward for `obj` for each token.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF under the 10 MiB limit with a long comment containing many delimiter-bounded `stream` tokens and no `obj` or `endobj` tokens. Each token triggers scans across much of the input, so preflight can perform quadratic CPU work in the API process before rejecting or starting the worker (OWASP A06:2025).

reviewers.summary: The changed tests cover the specified filter rejection cases and exact decoded limit. The preflight still performs repeated scans for `stream` tokens found inside comments.

findingList.message: Raw `stream` tokens in comments can trigger repeated full-prefix scans before the PDF reaches the worker, creating a CPU denial-of-service path (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: CheckStreamLimits finds each delimiter-bounded `stream` token, then calls LastIndexOfPdfToken from the start of the PDF to find a preceding `endobj`. These searches do not skip comments.
evidence.failureScenario: A submitted PDF under the 10,485,760-byte cap begins with a comment containing many delimiter-bounded `stream` tokens and has no `obj` or `endobj` tokens. Each token triggers another backward scan of the growing prefix before being skipped, causing quadratic CPU work in the API process. This is an availability risk (OWASP A06:2025).

reviewers.summary: The preflight has a reachable CPU denial-of-service path: repeated `stream` tokens in comments trigger repeated scans of the bounded input.

findingList.message: Untrusted `stream` tokens in comments can trigger repeated full-input scans, allowing a bounded PDF to consume excessive API CPU (OWASP A06:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: CheckStreamLimits searches for each delimiter-bounded `stream` token, then calls LastIndexOfPdfToken and FindPdfToken, which can each rescan a large part of the input. These scans do not skip PDF comments.
evidence.failureScenario: A presenter submits a PDF under the 10 MiB input limit with a long comment containing many delimiter-bounded `stream` tokens and no `obj` or `endobj` tokens. Each token triggers scans over much of the input, causing quadratic CPU work in the API before the document is rejected (OWASP A06:2025).
